newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 4.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on April 4. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Indonesia's Foreign Minister Ali Alatas has dismissed as "baseless rumours" reports that President Suharto was ill. Alatas blamed the foreign press for engineering the rumours about Suharto's health.

Publicly listed noodle maker PT Indofood Sukses Makmur of the Salim Group has obtained approval from its shareholders to buy 80 percent of the shares in each of its sister companies for 1.55 trillion rupiah ($651.26 million).

Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo has said Indonesia posted a trade surplus of $575.4 million in January against $916.2 million in December. He said January's trade surplus was 37.2 percent lower than in December but 38.1 percent higher compared to a year earlier.

The Attorney General's office have released two officials from the unrecognised the United Democratic Party of Indonesia (PUDI), Julius Usman and Saleh Abdulah, who were arrested last month on subversion charges. Their party had called for a boycott of the May 29 general elections. Party chairman, sacked legislator Sri Bintang Pamungkas, remains in custody.
